texts.exact_text: Wû Wang indicates great progress and success, while there will be advantage in being firm and correct. If (its subject and his action) be not correct, he will fall into errors, and it will not be advantageous for him to move in any direction.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, hexagram statement
texts.notes: Legge's title restored from the source statement.

texts.exact_text: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject free from all insincerity. His advance will be accompanied with good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, line 1

texts.exact_text: The second SIX, divided, shows one who reaps without having ploughed (that he might reap), and gathers the produce of his third year's fields without having cultivated them the first year for that end. To such a one there will be advantage in whatever direction he may move.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, line 2

texts.exact_text: The third SIX, divided, shows calamity happening to one who is free from insincerity; -- as in the case of an ox that has been tied up. A passer by finds it (and carries it off), while the people in the neighbourhood have the calamity (of being accused and. apprehended).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, line 3

texts.exact_text: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows (a case) in which, if its subject can remain firm and correct, there will be no error.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, line 4

texts.exact_text: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows one who is free from insincerity, and yet has fallen ill. Let him not use medicine, and he will have occasion for joy (in his recovery).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, line 5

texts.exact_text: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject free from insincerity, yet sure to fall into error, if he take action. (His action) will not be advantageous in any way.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, line 6

texts.exact_text:
Wû Wang is the symbol of being reckless, and often of being insincere; Wû Wang is descriptive of a state of entire freedom from such a condition; its subject is one who is entirely simple and sincere. The quality is characteristic of the action of Heaven, and of the highest style of humanity. In this hexagram we have an essay on this noble attribute. An absolute rectitude is essential to it. The nearer one comes to the ideal of the quality, the more powerful will be his influence, the greater his success. But let him see to it that he never swerve from being correct.

The first line is strong; at the commencement of the inner trigram ☳ Zhèn denoting movement, the action of its subject will very much characterise all the action set forth, and will itself be fortunate.

Line 2 is weak, central, and in its correct place. The quality may be predicated of it in its highest degree. There is an entire freedom in its subject from selfish or mercenary motive. He is good simply for goodness' sake. And things are so constituted that his action will be successful.

But calamity may also sometimes befal the best, and where there is this freedom from insincerity; and line 3 being weak, and in the place of an even line, lays its subject open to this misfortune. The people of the neighbourhood are of course entirely innocent.

Line 4 is the lowest in the trigram ☰ Qián of strength, and 1 is not a proper correlate, nor is the fourth the place for a strong line. Hence the paragraph must be understood as a caution.

Line 5 is strong, in the central place of honour, and has its proper correlate in 2. Hence its subject must possess the quality of the hexagram in perfection. And yet he shall he sick or in distress. But he need not be anxious. Without his efforts a way of escape for him will be opened.

Line 6 is at the top of the hexagram ䷘, and comes into the field when the action has run its course. He should be still, and not initiate any fresh movement. 无妄 ䷘
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 25; scan-backed transcription p. 109, notes

texts.exact_text: 无妄：元亨。利貞。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 易經卦辭

texts.exact_text: 无妄，剛自外來，而為主於內。動而健，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之命也。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。无妄之往，何之矣？ 天命不佑，行矣哉？
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 彖

texts.exact_text: 天下雷行，物與无妄；先王以茂對時，育萬物。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 大象

texts.exact_text: 初九：无妄，往吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 爻 1

texts.exact_text: 无妄之往，得志也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 小象 1

texts.exact_text: 六二：不耕穫，不菑畬，則利有攸往。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 爻 2

texts.exact_text: 不耕穫，未富也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 小象 2

texts.exact_text: 六三：无妄之災，或系之牛，行人之得，邑人之災。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 爻 3

texts.exact_text: 行人得牛，邑人災也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 小象 3

texts.exact_text: 九四：可貞，无咎。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 爻 4

texts.exact_text: 可貞无咎，固有之也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 小象 4

texts.exact_text: 九五：无妄之疾，勿藥有喜。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 爻 5

texts.exact_text: 无妄之藥，不可試也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 小象 5

texts.exact_text: 上九：无妄，行有眚，无攸利。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 爻 6

texts.exact_text: 无妄之行，窮之災也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/无妄; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 25, 小象 6

texts.exact_text: In Wû Wang we have the strong (first) line come from the outer (trigram ☰), and become in the inner trigram ☳ lord (of the whole figure); we have (the attributes of) motive power and strength; we have the strong line (of the fifth place) in the central position, and responded to (by the weak second): -- there will be 'great progress proceeding from correctness; such is the appointment of Heaven. 'If (its subject and his action) be not correct, he will fall into errors, and it will not be advantageous for him to move in any direction:' -- whither can he (who thinks he is) free from all insincerity, (and yet is as here described) proceed? Can anything be done (advantageously) by him whom the (will and) appointment of Heaven do not help?
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix I, Hexagram 25, p. 234

texts.exact_text: Wû Wang The thunder rolls all under the sky, and to (every)thing there is given (its nature), free from all insincerity. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, (made their regulations) in complete accordance with the seasons, thereby nourishing all things.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 25, p. 300

texts.exact_text: When 'he who is free from insincerity makes any movement,' he will get what he desires.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 25, line 1, p. 300

texts.exact_text: 'He reaps without having ploughed:' -- (the thought of) riches to be got had not risen (in his mind).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 25, line 2, p. 300

texts.exact_text: 'The passer-by gets the ox:' -- this proves a calamity to the people of the neighbourhood.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 25, line 3, p. 300

texts.exact_text: 'If he can remain firm and correct there will be no error:' -- he firmly holds fast (his correctness).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 25, line 4, p. 300

texts.exact_text: 'Medicine in the case of one who is free from insincerity!' -- it should not be tried (at all).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 25, line 5, p. 300

texts.exact_text: 'The action (in this case) of one who is free from insincerity' will occasion the calamity arising from action (when the time for it is) exhausted.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 25, line 6, p. 300
